purpose: Current project map for keeping Graft small, dependency-free, contributor-friendly, and release-ready.

current_state.summary: Graft is a dependency-free Python 3.10+ CLI that scans a directory, writes a JSON manifest, and refreshes Markdown inventory tables between stable markers.

planning_principles: Keep runtime dependencies at zero unless a feature clearly cannot be built with the Python standard library.
Prefer small, reviewable changes over large rewrites.
Keep public-facing README content concise and move deeper process notes into docs/.
Protect human-authored Markdown outside generated inventory markers.
Make contributor tasks concrete, labeled, and testable.
Use check mode and tests as the guardrails for generated content behavior.
Keep Windows, PowerShell, and low-memory workflows in mind.

project_plan.name: Foundation and repository posture
project_plan.goal: Make the repository safe, understandable, and ready for contributors before feature expansion.

tasks.title: Choose and add a project license
tasks.rationale: Apache-2.0 is selected and documented so users and contributors know the reuse terms.
acceptance_criteria: Add a LICENSE file at the repository root.
Update README.md and project metadata with the selected license.
Confirm the chosen license matches the maintainer's intended reuse posture.

tasks.title: Keep support documentation organized under docs/
tasks.rationale: Support docs live under docs/ while the root remains a clean landing page.
acceptance_criteria: Move notes and contributing material into docs/.
Keep root-level support-doc duplicates removed.
Update CLI defaults and inventories so docs/notes.md is the notes target.

tasks.title: Document issue labels and project taxonomy
tasks.rationale: Consistent labels keep issues easy to sort and contributors aware of work type.
acceptance_criteria: Add docs/issue_labels.md.
Document label categories for priority, type, status, and miscellaneous states.
Use the label taxonomy when creating future issues.

project_plan.name: Documentation and onboarding
project_plan.goal: Give users and contributors enough context to run, understand, and improve the project without needing private chat history.

tasks.title: Add example workflows and CLI usage docs
tasks.rationale: Copy-paste examples make the CLI easier to understand and give new contributors safe starting points.
acceptance_criteria: Add docs/examples.md or an equivalent examples document.
Document copy-pasteable commands.
Include examples for scanning a repository, scanning a subfolder, custom output targets, and using check mode.

tasks.title: Maintain architecture documentation
tasks.rationale: Architecture notes explain the flow from CLI parsing to scanning, rendering, writing, dry-run previews, and check-mode validation.
acceptance_criteria: Add docs/architecture.md.
Describe the core flow and InventoryGenerator responsibilities.
Keep architecture notes updated when core behavior changes.

tasks.title: Refresh docs after completed roadmap and summary-extraction work
tasks.rationale: The docs should describe completed dry-run, check-mode, custom-target, summary-extraction, lint-policy, and CI work as current behavior, not future work.
acceptance_criteria: Update docs/architecture.md to describe current summary extraction and testing coverage.
Update docs/ROADMAP.md so completed work is not listed as future work.
Refresh docs/suggestions.json so remaining release-readiness work points to issues 15 and 16 and completed issues are visible.
Keep README.md and docs/notes.md inventory blocks current.

tasks.title: Refresh README and notes inventories after documentation changes
tasks.rationale: Generated inventories should reflect the current docs layout and summaries without overwriting human-written Markdown outside stable markers.
acceptance_criteria: Run or manually apply the generated inventory update after docs change.
Ensure README.md and docs/notes.md inventories list the current tracked project files.
Do not commit generated manifest.json.

project_plan.name: CLI safety and usability
project_plan.goal: Make Graft safer to preview, easier to verify, and more pleasant to use in real repositories.

tasks.title: Implement optional dry-run mode for CLI
tasks.rationale: Dry-run mode lets users preview manifest and Markdown inventory changes without touching files.
acceptance_criteria: Add a --dry-run CLI option.
Print which files would be created or updated.
Do not modify files while dry-run mode is active.
Add tests that prove files are left unchanged.

tasks.title: Decide whether generated manifest.json should be tracked
tasks.rationale: manifest.json remains generated output and ignored by default unless a future fixture intentionally tracks a manifest.
acceptance_criteria: Record the tracking policy in documentation.
Keep manifest.json ignored unless a tracked example is intentionally added.
Update README.md or docs/examples.md with the chosen guidance.

tasks.title: Expand tests for check mode
tasks.rationale: Check mode is the core CI guardrail and is covered for passing and stale-output cases.
acceptance_criteria: Test check mode returns zero when generated files are current.
Test check mode returns non-zero when Markdown inventory is stale.
Test check mode returns non-zero when manifest output is missing or stale.

tasks.title: Add tests for custom README, notes, and manifest targets
tasks.rationale: Custom output paths are part of the CLI contract and now have regression coverage.
acceptance_criteria: Test --readme writes to a custom Markdown file.
Test --notes writes to a custom Markdown file.
Test --manifest writes JSON to a custom path.

project_plan.name: Summary extraction and quality gates
project_plan.goal: Improve inventory usefulness and validation while keeping the project lightweight.

tasks.title: Improve summaries for additional file types
tasks.rationale: Summaries now cover more safe text formats without adding parsers or runtime dependencies.
acceptance_criteria: Keep summary extraction dependency-free.
Cover JSON, TOML, and comment-based file types with tests.
Preserve fallback behavior when no clear summary exists.

tasks.title: Round out lightweight summary extraction edge cases
tasks.rationale: YAML-style metadata and JSDoc-style block comments are supported with simple heuristics and focused tests.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime dependencies remain zero.
Python 3.10+ compatibility is preserved.
Tests cover YAML-style summary extraction and block-comment summaries.

tasks.title: Document lightweight lint and format policy
tasks.rationale: Ruff is documented as optional local developer tooling and is not a runtime or enforced CI dependency.
acceptance_criteria: Document optional local lint guidance.
Keep CI dependency-light.
Avoid adding mandatory runtime tooling.

tasks.title: Split CI into focused validation jobs
tasks.rationale: CI now separates lightweight smoke checks from the Python 3.10, 3.11, and 3.12 unit-test matrix.
acceptance_criteria: Run syntax and CLI help smoke checks.
Run unit tests across supported Python versions.
Keep jobs readable for contributors.

project_plan.name: Packaging and release readiness
project_plan.goal: Prepare Graft for safe tagging, installation, and possible publication once release decisions are documented.

tasks.title: Define versioning and release process
tasks.rationale: The package has version metadata, but maintainers still need a clear process for bumps, tags, and release notes.
acceptance_criteria: Document when to bump patch, minor, or major versions.
Document a release checklist in docs/maintainer_workflow.md.
Document when to create a Git tag.
Keep pyproject.toml version aligned with releases.

tasks.title: Confirm package name and publication readiness
tasks.rationale: Before publication, maintainers should confirm the package name, console command, and install guidance.
acceptance_criteria: Confirm graft-inventory is the intended package name.
Confirm the console script name remains graft.
Document local or editable install guidance.
Defer actual publishing unless explicitly chosen later.

tasks.title: Add release-focused CI checks when ready
tasks.rationale: Basic CI exists now. Release CI can wait until package publication is a real goal.
acceptance_criteria: Add package build validation if publication becomes active work.
Validate metadata with standard Python packaging tools if development dependencies are acceptable.
Keep runtime dependency-free even if development tooling is added.

project_plan.name: Future feature polish
project_plan.goal: Add useful features only after the core contract is stable and well-tested.

tasks.title: Consider manifest comparison mode
tasks.rationale: Comparing old and new manifests could help maintainers understand what changed between scans.
acceptance_criteria: Define expected input format for old and new manifests.
Print added, removed, and changed files clearly.
Add tests for comparison output.

tasks.title: Consider machine-readable check output
tasks.rationale: JSON output for check mode could make Graft easier to integrate into dashboards or bots.
acceptance_criteria: Add an opt-in flag such as --json.
Keep normal human-readable output unchanged by default.
Document schema and add tests.

Complete issue #15 by documenting versioning rules, tagging guidance, and a release checklist.
Complete issue #16 by confirming package name, console command, install guidance, and publication posture.
Keep README.md and docs/notes.md inventories refreshed when tracked files or summaries change.

maintenance_notes: Keep this file hand-editable and dependency-free.
When an issue closes, update the matching task status.
